content: The initial source of energy for food webs and food chains is the Sun. Solar energy is captured by primary producers, primarily plants, algae, and some bacteria, through the process of photosynthesis. During photosynthesis, these organisms convert sunlight into chemical energy in the form of glucose, which can then be used to support their growth and metabolism. From there, energy is transferred through various trophic levels in an ecosystem as these producers are consumed by herbivores (primary consumers), which in turn may be consumed by carnivores (secondary and tertiary consumers), and so on. Decomposers also play a crucial role by breaking down dead organisms and recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
